title: Trump Refers Habba's Claim of a Missing Kennedy Center Donation Under Grenell to White House Counsel
institution: John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts; White House Counsel's Office
status: Under White House counsel and Kennedy Center review; allegation unproven and denied
what_changed:
Alina Habba, President Trump's former personal attorney, told Trump in the Oval Office that Ric Grenell, who ran the Kennedy Center from February 2025 until March 2026, **failed to deposit a multimillion-dollar donation to the center that, she said, Turkish businessman Turhan Mildon, who later became her husband, arranged in May 2025.** Axios, citing four senior administration officials and three other people briefed on the dispute, reported on Oct. 14, 2026 that Trump referred the allegation to White House Counsel Will Scharf to look into. According to Habba's account, Grenell persuaded Mildon in the spring of 2025 to fold the donation into a $17.6 million wire transfer for a business deal involving a U.S. company. Habba first put the donation at $17 million, then at $5.6 million; Axios's sources also described it as nearly $6 million. Grenell called the claim "absurd" and a lie, saying "I've never received any payment from him at all." A senior administration official said the claims were only allegations. When Axios reported, counsel had asked for documentation but received none; the New York Times later reported that Mildon's lawyer sent Scharf text messages and a wire transfer receipt that night. Grenell denies sending a text attributed to him, and no outlet has verified the documents. Kennedy Center staff who searched for the donation in late 2025 could not find it; the only record they found showed Mildon owed a $270,000 pledge, which he paid on Oct. 13, 2026, after the New York Times asked about it. The center says it is reviewing relevant pledges and funds. The dispute reportedly grew out of Grenell and Mildon's shared interests in Venezuela.

Update 2026-10-21: Axios reported on Oct. 19, 2026 that the White House counsel is investigating a May 3, 2025 text, supplied by Mildon's attorneys and denied by Grenell, that reads: "Once the money comes to the company here, I will arrange the donation to Kennedy Centre [sic], and you'll be joining the VIP events and get close with the administration, even with POTUS." Mildon alleges that at Grenell's direction he wired $17.6 million to Texas Armament & Technology (TXAT), a Houston-based defense company, to be split between a Congo deal and nearly $6 million for the Kennedy Center; sources told Axios the White House also received a May 29, 2025 financial record showing the transfer. Contrary to what Habba first told Trump, the money did not appear to come from Mildon's own account: a White House official told Axios it was wired from Congo's "Ministère des Finances" in Kinshasa, and the New York Times reported it came from a bank account affiliated with the Congolese government. Mildon has told the Times he serves as an adviser to the Congolese president and holds a Congolese diplomatic passport. Grenell acknowledged consulting for TXAT in 2024 but says he had no connection to it when the transfer was made and denies any connection to the transfer. Habba and Mildon married in September 2026; Will Scharf, the White House counsel leading the inquiry, attended the wedding, the Times reported.

primary_proponent.name: Ric Grenell
primary_proponent.role: Former president of the Kennedy Center (February 2025 to March 2026)
primary_proponent.note: Accused by Alina Habba of failing to deposit a donation she says Turhan Mildon, now her husband, arranged; he denies it, denies sending the May 2025 text attributed to him, and says he never received any payment from Mildon.

estimated_impact.summary: If true, a donation of several million dollars intended for the Kennedy Center never reached it; if false, the claim is a dispute among Trump allies now before the White House counsel.

figures.value: $5.6 million to nearly $6 million (first stated as $17 million)
figures.source: Habba's account to the White House, as reported by Axios

figures.metric: Wire transfer the donation was allegedly folded into
figures.value: $17.6 million, wired to Texas Armament & Technology (TXAT), per a May 29, 2025 financial record
figures.source: Habba's and Mildon's accounts and a financial record given to the White House, as reported by Axios and the New York Times

figures.value: Reportedly Congo's Finance Ministry in Kinshasa (a Congolese government-affiliated account), apparently not Mildon's own account
figures.source: A White House official, per Axios (Oct. 19, 2026); people familiar with the matter, per the New York Times (Oct. 17, 2026)

figures.metric: Pledge Kennedy Center records show Mildon owed, paid Oct. 13, 2026
figures.source: Kennedy Center records, as reported by Axios and the New York Times

estimated_impact.caveat: Every dollar figure here comes from Habba's side or from anonymous officials; no audit, filing or official finding confirms any money went missing, and the center's own search found only a $270,000 pledge.

confidence_note: LOW confidence on the underlying allegation, HIGH confidence that it was made and referred. Axios broke the story from four senior administration officials and three other insiders, and the New York Times and Washington Post confirmed the Oval Office account independently, with Grenell's on-record denial. The New York Times reported that Mildon's lawyer sent Scharf text messages and a wire transfer receipt on Oct. 14; Grenell disputes at least one of the texts, and no outlet has verified the documents. Frame it as an unproven accusation under internal review, not as a finding of missing money. Update 2026-10-21: Axios reviewed the May 2025 text Grenell denies sending, and a source said Scharf plans to verify its digital footprint. A White House official says the $17.6 million came from Congo's Finance Ministry rather than Mildon, contradicting Habba's first account; the Times reported that Scharf, who leads the inquiry, attended the Mildons' wedding.

section_summaries.what_changed: Trump sent Alina Habba's claim that Ric Grenell never deposited a Kennedy Center donation, tied to a $17.6M wire reportedly from a Congo government account, to his White House counsel.
section_summaries.estimated_impact: Millions meant for the Kennedy Center may be unaccounted for, but the only record the center found is a $270,000 pledge, paid Oct. 13, 2026.
section_summaries.confidence_note: The allegation and referral are well reported; the missing money and the May 2025 text Grenell denies sending are unverified, and the wire's source undercuts Habba's first account.
